title: Data ownership: which layer owns which byte
description: The catalogue ADR-0010 asks for. That decision splits the system into 'user intent' and 'executable truth' and then says the boundary needs a list -- which key is intent, which is observation, which is secret -- 'that must be maintained as data rather than remembered' (docs/adr/0010-data-split-extension-intent-connector-truth.md:66-69). This file is that list. It is data, not a table in a document, because a table in a document drifts: the legacy tree already contains three stores whose contents overlap (docs/audit/04-data-model-and-options-envelope.md section 1), a sync path that strips four value keys and forgot the fifth (SEC-1), and a state key holding a Gist token that no strip rule can reach (SEC-5). Every row here is checked by scripts/verify.mjs against the envelope-key registry, the command allowlist and the sync strip set, so a new entity, a new credential field or a new command has to declare where its bytes rest before the harness will stay green.

planes.process: the extension: service worker, options page, popup
planes.owns: user intent, and every copy of an observation the UI is showing right now
planes.diesWith: the browser profile; a wipe of chrome.storage.local destroys everything in it except the IndexedDB mirrors
planes.note: chrome.storage.local is the durable half. The pseudo-localStorage state store and its single-blob IndexedDB mirror are the least durable part of this plane (docs/audit/05-storage-sync-and-migration.md section 3).

planes.process: nexora-connector (Go), plus the files it writes in the user profile
planes.owns: executable truth: keystore values, the compiled config and its hash, health history, the fetched-feed cache, the diagnostics ring, the Core binary and its receipts
planes.diesWith: the Connector's per-user directory, which outlives both the extension and a Core upgrade
planes.note: Nothing in this plane syncs. It has no account, no server, and no cloud (docs/architecture/21-system-context.md section 9).

planes.process: Xray Core, a child process the Connector started
planes.owns: the config file it was handed, in plaintext, for as long as it is allowed to run
planes.diesWith: the process; the file is a cache and is deleted when Core stops
planes.note: Core is not a data owner in the user-visible sense: everything it holds is re-derivable from intent plus keystore, which is exactly why losing it must never need a migration.

classes.rule: Something the user created or edited. Only the extension may write it; the Connector MUST NOT create, reorder or invent intent (ADR-0010 rule 6).
A transient copy of a payload that had not finished arriving. Local-only, hard-expiring, and allowed to hold secret values because it is the ingest path.
A deliberate copy of everything, taken to be restored from. Inherits the secrets of whatever it copied, so it is local-only.
Credential material. Exists only as a keystore blob in the Connector plane; everywhere else it is a reference or a mask.
What the Connector measured or produced. The browser may hold a copy for display and MUST treat it as an observation, never as its own truth (ADR-0010 rule 2).
A value computed from other data, stored next to its source for speed. Always re-derivable, so it may be deleted at any time and MUST NOT be the only copy of anything the user made.
Program bytes and the records that authorise them: the pin document, the installed binary, install receipts. Not user data, never exported, verified before executed.

stores.location: one key per Server, UUID-suffixed
stores.holds: transport, address, port, security, the flow and stream settings, and keystore references for every credential
stores.writer: the options UI, through the typed mutators; profile.import may replace them as a set
stores.purge: profile.remove, which also schedules the keystore-delete side effect (docs/architecture/26-command-surface.md)
stores.bound: one storage item per Server; a Server is bounded by server.schema.json, not by the number of Servers
stores.mitigation: keystore
stores.check: LIVE-19: the references survive, the values do not, and the UI says so

stores.location: one key per ConnectorProfile intent document
stores.holds: the intent that compiles to exactly one loopback FixedProfile (packages/schema/connector-profile.schema.json)
stores.purge: profile.remove
stores.bound: one storage item per profile
stores.mitigation: keystore
stores.check: LIVE-05 and the golden configs: intent compiles, it does not become truth by itself

stores.location: one key per RoutingPolicy
stores.holds: rule order, domains, keywords, CIDRs, proxy groups -- the two-plane routing model of docs/architecture/28-routing-model.md
stores.purge: profile.remove / policy delete
stores.bound: one storage item per policy; rule count bounded by routing-policy.schema.json
stores.mitigation: none needed: routing data is not credential data
stores.check: LIVE-05 through LIVE-09: the compiled form is checked, not the intent's size

stores.location: one key per SubscriptionSource
stores.holds: the fetch policy, the display URL with its query dropped, the format the last refresh resolved and the extension wrote back, and the two references (urlRef, headersRef) that hold the credential-shaped halves
stores.writer: the options UI creates it; subscription.refresh NEVER writes this key -- the source is intent and the Connector does not own intent. The one field of it the refresh corrects is format: the extension persists the resolved value from refreshed[].format into the source it owns, so auto never survives storage (docs/architecture/34-data-split.md section 6) -- the extension holds the pen, the Connector only reports the verdict
stores.purge: profile.remove, plus keystore.purge for its references
stores.bound: one storage item; the body it points at is bounded by limits.maxBytes, not by this key
stores.mitigation: keystore: url and headers travel as references (docs/architecture/29 section 4)
stores.check: LIVE-12: a failed refresh keeps the last good set; LIVE-19 covers the inert-reference case

stores.location: one scalar key
stores.holds: Connector settings: install channel, loopback ports, timeouts, log level
stores.purge: reset paths only
stores.bound: one storage item, schema-bounded
stores.mitigation: none needed
stores.check: LIVE-21 and LIVE-20: installChannel is read where the bytes are installed, not where the user clicked

stores.location: one scalar key
stores.holds: the user's fail-open/fail-closed choice and its grace and hard-cap numbers
stores.purge: reset paths only
stores.bound: one storage item, failure-policy.schema.json bounded
stores.mitigation: none needed
stores.check: LIVE-11: the resolution is applied from this intent; the countdown is recomputed from Connector state (docs/architecture/30 section 11)

stores.location: one scalar key; the authoritative copy is the Connector's pin document
stores.holds: the user's chosen pin: tag, assets, hashes, signature policy. Sync-eligible because it is a public statement about a public release; the copy here is what the UI displays and what a support bundle can show, never what the installer trusts.
stores.writer: the options UI on an explicit upgrade action (ADR-0019 rule 6)
stores.purge: replaced by the next verified pin; never deleted, because an absent pin means no Core may run
stores.bound: one storage item; assets are enumerated, not streamed
stores.mitigation: not secret: a pin is a public statement about a public release
stores.check: LIVE-02 and LIVE-20: the copy that matters is verified against upstream before anything is executed

stores.location: one key per interrupted import
stores.holds: the accumulated raw payload of a profile.import that was still being reassembled when the worker died -- the only NEXORA namespace in the browser plane allowed to contain a secret value
stores.writer: the chunk receiver in the extension
stores.purge: expiresAt, and cleared as soon as profile.import is acknowledged; keystore.purge scope 'orphaned' collects a buffer whose subscription is gone
stores.bound: body maxLength 8388608; chunkCount maxItems 1024; lifetime bounded by expiresAt
stores.mitigation: localOnly: the namespace is syncEligible false and diagnostics.get never reads it
stores.check: LIVE-18 covers the ingest half; the frame gap rule is checked by the chunk-order assertion over framing.json

stores.location: one key per pre-migration snapshot, timestamped
stores.holds: a copy of the whole envelope, therefore a copy of whatever was in it; keyCount must be non-zero (packages/schema/envelope-backup.schema.json)
stores.writer: the migration runner, before it destroys anything (ADR-0014)
stores.purge: explicit user action; retention is a policy question, not a code question
stores.bound: one storage item per snapshot; the number of snapshots kept is open (docs/architecture/40-open-decisions.md)
stores.mitigation: localOnly: syncEligible false, and it is not part of an export unless the user exports a snapshot deliberately
stores.check: LIVE-14: a snapshot that cannot restore is the failure this row exists to prevent

stores.location: '+' + name, one key per OmegaPac profile, plus the bare schemaVersion stamp
stores.holds: FixedProfile, PacProfile, SwitchProfile, RuleListProfile and their derived fields (pacScript, ruleList, sha256, lastUpdate) stored beside the source data (docs/audit/04-data-model-and-options-envelope.md section 3 rule 3)
stores.writer: the frozen legacy engine -- ADR-0002: NEXORA does not rewrite what works
stores.purge: the engine's own delete paths; a removed '+' key is a change class, not just a missing key
stores.bound: unbounded in practice: unlimitedStorage is granted in both manifests (omega-target-chromium-extension/overlay/manifest.json:44, omega-target-chromium-extension/overlay/manifest-firefox.json:43)
stores.mitigation: syncExcludedValueKeys: the strip set carries headers and auth, which is the SEC-1 closure and the reason the legacy four-key list was wrong
stores.check: LIVE-14 for fidelity; LIVE-22 for 'nothing credential-shaped left this store'

stores.location: '-' + name: the sixteen keys the engine reads or writes, eleven of them shipped by default
stores.holds: quick-switch lists, startup profile, confirm-deletion, customCss, monitorWebRequests, builtinProfiles, downloadInterval
stores.writer: the engine and the legacy options page
stores.purge: reset paths
stores.bound: one storage item each; -customCss is excluded from sync today
stores.mitigation: none needed: no credential field is defined here
stores.check: LIVE-22, as a grep over a real dump rather than a reading of this row

stores.location: pseudo-localStorage under the 'omega.local.' prefix, mirrored as ONE IndexedDB blob
stores.holds: availableProfiles, syncOptions, the log tail, and -- the reason this row is not simply legacy trivia -- gistToken
stores.purge: the debug reset and the onInstalled wipe, both of which clear the IndexedDB mirror wholesale
stores.bound: unbounded blob; every set rewrites the whole map (docs/audit/05-storage-sync-and-migration.md section 3)
stores.mitigation: keystore: the target placement is a 'sync'-entity reference; the value never sits in the browser plane (docs/architecture/32 section 14)
stores.check: LIVE-22; the durability defect it inherits is recorded, not fixed, in docs/architecture/35-schema-versioning-migration.md §3

stores.location: tempProfileState
stores.holds: the temporary profile and whether it is active -- a rule the user made for now, not history
stores.purge: the browser clears it with the session
stores.bound: two keys
stores.mitigation: none needed
stores.check: LIVE-13: a service-worker restart must not resurrect it and must not lose the applied proxy decision
stores.note: The manifest floor predates chrome.storage.session availability, and the legacy code has no guard (docs/audit/05-storage-sync-and-migration.md section 3, session-store caveat). NEXORA MUST NOT repeat an unguarded store.

stores.location: one key: zeroOmegaSync
stores.holds: the built-in sync configuration: gistId, syncUsername, backend, last commit -- and, today, gistToken written whole (omega-target/src/options_sync.coffee:240-242)
stores.writer: the options page and background.coffee's sync re-init path
stores.purge: chrome.storage.sync is cleared by the onInstalled wipe (docs/audit/05-storage-sync-and-migration.md section 7 row 3)
stores.bound: the browser account sync quota, which is the only quota the legacy tree actually fails on (options_sync.coffee:157-170 marks profiles 'disabled')
stores.mitigation: none (open item, docs/architecture/40-open-decisions.md): the strip list cannot reach this key, so SEC-5's built-in-sync write stays open until the token moves to the keystore and this blob shrinks to a reference
stores.check: LIVE-22 is the row that would fail today, which is the honest reason it exists

stores.location: the 'sync-store' object store
stores.holds: the local mirror of what was pushed to Gist or WebDAV, plus the commit pointer
stores.purge: sync reset, which also clears the remote (docs/audit/05-storage-sync-and-migration.md section 7 row 9)
stores.bound: grows with the envelope; no compaction exists
stores.mitigation: syncExcludedValueKeys: what is mirrored is what was stripped on the way out
stores.check: LIVE-12 for last-good behaviour; the destructive-reset path is a migration concern (docs/architecture/35-schema-versioning-migration.md §12)

stores.location: the 'log-store' object store and the 'log' state key
stores.holds: diagnostic entries and lastError, exported today by a UI button
stores.purge: the debug reset
stores.bound: unbounded today (docs/audit/11-security-findings.md SEC-7); the NEXORA replacement is 2000 records and 2 MiB in the same medium, capped three ways at once (packages/schema/observability.json#/sinks, docs/architecture/36-observability.md §5 and §10)
stores.mitigation: sink masking: the redaction table is built from live keystore contents and applied at every sink, which is docs/architecture/32 section 8's replacement for the legacy name-keyed list
stores.check: LIVE-10 greps an exported log; LIVE-22 greps a storage dump

stores.location: the Svelte stores holding the last config.snapshot, core.status and connector.health
stores.holds: masked renderings and a hash, for as long as the page is open
stores.purge: page unload
stores.bound: one response per component per mount
stores.mitigation: sink masking
stores.check: LIVE-04 is the reason a copy for display must never be treated as a verdict: 'healthy' has a definition this row does not own

stores.location: %LOCALAPPDATA%\NEXORA\keystore, one protected blob per secret (ADR-0011 rule 1)
stores.holds: every credential value in the system, plus the HMAC key that mints fingerprints
stores.writer: the Connector only -- profile.import credentials and subscription.refresh are the two paths that mint a reference
stores.purge: keystore.purge by scope, including 'orphaned'; profile.remove's keystore-delete side effect
stores.bound: one blob per entity field; growth is bounded by the entity count, not by traffic
stores.mitigation: keystore: this is the store; ADR-0011 decides the mechanism, docs/architecture/32 decides what may point at it
stores.check: LIVE-18: round trip, rotation, purge by scope, and the refusal to strand an applied config

stores.location: the Connector's per-user config directory (docs/architecture/34-data-split.md section 7's layout: %LOCALAPPDATA%\NEXORA\config on Windows), owner-only ACL, one stable file name -- the same name every apply renames over
stores.holds: plaintext credentials -- the declared exception (packages/schema/envelope-keys.schema.json at secretReferences.atRest) because Xray cannot be handed references
stores.writer: ConfigCompiler, then a rename into place
stores.purge: core.stop and Connector shutdown; it is re-derivable from intent plus keystore, so it is never backed up and never exported
stores.bound: one file. Replacing a config is a rename over the same name (doc 27 section 8), so the previous bytes are gone with the rename and no collector exists -- a hash-derived name would have needed the GC that ODEC-26 owns and would have handed Core a new path every apply
stores.mitigation: lifetime: owner-only for the window in which Core may run, and maskedConfig is the only version that leaves
stores.check: LIVE-18 owns the lifetime and the ACL; LIVE-03 owns the loopback-only bind inside it

stores.location: a small state file: applied config hash, selected profile, last start PID, last exit
stores.holds: what is true right now, which is what config.snapshot and core.status report
stores.purge: rewritten on every apply; a corrupt file means recompile, not data loss
stores.bound: a handful of fields
stores.mitigation: not secret: hashes and identifiers only
stores.check: LIVE-13: after a browser restart the Connector must still be able to say what it applied

stores.location: a ring per server id
stores.holds: probe results, latencies, failure streaks -- the data behind every green or red mark
stores.purge: ring eviction; ids are reused across refreshes so history survives a feed update (docs/architecture/29 section 8)
stores.bound: ring-buffered by design: a user cannot fill a disk by probing more
stores.mitigation: not secret: no probe result carries a credential, and the egress probe answer is an IP the user already knows
stores.check: LIVE-04: a health row is only allowed to mean what that row says it means

stores.location: a bounded cache per subscription id, keyed by content hash
stores.holds: the last fetched feed body and its parse outcome -- a stream of user UUIDs and often a token in the URL that fetched it
stores.purge: replaced by the next successful refresh; expired on source delete with keystore.purge scope
stores.bound: limits.maxBytes, default 2 MiB, ceiling 8 MiB (docs/architecture/29 section 3); the legacy path had no cap at all
stores.mitigation: localOnly: never handed to diagnostics.get, never crosses the pipe toward the browser (docs/architecture/29 section 2)
stores.check: LIVE-12 keeps the last good version; LIVE-10 is the grep that proves the body never surfaces

stores.location: a ring buffer, exported on request through diagnostics.get
stores.holds: events, decisions the failure policy took, the applied hash, redacted log lines
stores.purge: ring eviction; nothing here is durable by design
stores.bound: size-bounded and ring-buffered, stated in the command summary itself (packages/schema/protocol/commands/diagnostics.get.json)
stores.mitigation: sink masking: values are destroyed where they leave the process, keyed on the live keystore contents
stores.check: LIVE-10 greps this output; docs/architecture/36 owns the format it arrives in

stores.location: a logs directory inside the Connector's state directory, beside the applied-state file
stores.holds: the same records as the ring, appended before the process can die, so the run that ended is the one that described itself
stores.purge: rotation at the byte cap, deletion at the age cap and the file count, whichever comes first (docs/architecture/36-observability.md §10)
stores.bound: 5 MiB per file, 5 files, aged by telemetry.retentionDays -- all three caps in packages/schema/observability.json#/sinks
stores.mitigation: sink masking before the write: the value-keyed pass runs in the same render that produces the ring copy, so the file and the ring cannot disagree about what was redacted (docs/architecture/32-secrets-keystore-masking.md §8)
stores.check: LIVE-10 greps an exported log; docs/architecture/36-observability.md §5 states why a memory-only ring cannot answer why the Connector exited

stores.location: the path the Compiler writes into the Core config's log section, inside the Connector's state directory
stores.holds: Xray's own error log. It holds no access log: the Compiler states access as 'none' rather than leaving it to an upstream default (docs/architecture/36-observability.md §9)
stores.purge: Xray rotates its own files on an interval this design does not configure; the Connector caps how many exist, ages them, and tail-reads them into the ring
stores.bound: 1 MiB per file, 2 files, plus the cap on how much of it a single diagnostics.get section may return
stores.mitigation: captured whole and passed through the value-keyed mask on the way into the ring; the file itself is read-only to NEXORA, which is why the access log is switched off at the source rather than filtered on the way out
stores.check: docs/architecture/36-observability.md §9 owns the decision; LIVE-10 greps the ring copy of these lines

stores.location: a bounded map from client id to the response that was given
stores.holds: enough to answer a replay without repeating an effect (ADR-0008)
stores.purge: eviction; a probe result is never cached at all
stores.bound: bounded window; replay outside it is a fresh call, which is why 'replayed' is a response field
stores.mitigation: sink masking: a cached response is a response, and gets masked like one
stores.check: the replay fixtures in packages/schema/fixtures/protocol/ and LIVE-01's session half

stores.location: the per-user install root named by the pin document, never the extension directory
stores.holds: the executable that carries the user's traffic, plus the receipts that say it was verified
stores.writer: the installer, only after signature then hash then size then traversal checks
stores.purge: the rollback GC bounded by retainedPreviousVersions
stores.bound: retainedPreviousVersions versions on disk
stores.mitigation: not secret, and never in the archive: ADR-0019 keeps it out of git and out of the zip
stores.check: LIVE-02, LIVE-20, LIVE-21

stores.location: the pin document the host resolved at startup, beside the binary
stores.holds: the authoritative copy of what is permitted to run -- the browser-plane copy is display only
stores.writer: the installer, atomically with the binary it authorises
stores.purge: replaced by the next verified pin; the previous one is kept while its binary is kept
stores.bound: one document per retained version
stores.mitigation: not secret: a pin is a public claim about a public release
stores.check: LIVE-20: upgrade re-verifies before it switches, which is only meaningful if the pin and the binary change together

stores.location: the path Core was handed on the command line
stores.holds: the same bytes as compiled-config: Core's view of what it may do
stores.writer: nobody -- it is read by Core and written by the Connector
stores.purge: deleted with the config lifetime; an unclean kill leaves it, which is the open item docs/architecture/32 section 13 and docs/architecture/33 share
stores.bound: one file
stores.mitigation: lifetime: owner-only, bounded, never exported -- see compiled-config above
stores.check: LIVE-03 is the row that proves what it binds; the assertion that it is not writable through Core is ADR-0008's, not this row's

movements.payload: intent documents: profiles, servers, routing, settings -- references, never values
movements.onOverflow: chunked-envelope, reassembled and hash-checked before anything is replaced
movements.check: LIVE-05 through LIVE-09; the chunk rules are asserted over framing.json

movements.payload: credentials[]: the single field in the whole command surface that may receive a secret value
movements.bound: writeOnly true, per-frame entry count bounded, forbidden on chunked frames because reassembly lives where DPAPI does not reach
movements.onOverflow: refused, not staged: an oversized import is a bug in the caller, not a size problem
movements.check: LIVE-18; the 'exactly one field' rule is asserted in scripts/verify.mjs

movements.payload: the feed body, parsed inside the Connector so that its user UUIDs and token-bearing URL never enter a browser process
movements.onOverflow: the refresh fails and the last good set stays applied (docs/architecture/29 section 9)
movements.check: LIVE-12; SSRF-2 owns the address guard

movements.payload: the applied config with field names preserved and values destroyed, plus the hash and the drift verdict
movements.bound: one snapshot per call; the mask literal is fixed-width so length is not leaked either
movements.onOverflow: the caller asks for less: a snapshot is a summary surface, not a dump
movements.check: LIVE-10 greps this output for a pinned secret and expects nothing

movements.payload: state, PID, applied hash, lastExit, the grace countdown's inputs
movements.bound: a handful of fields per call
movements.check: LIVE-11 and LIVE-13: the browser recomputes deadlines from this, it does not store its own copy of the truth

movements.payload: state transitions: core.exited, config.applied, integrity.mismatch, subscription.updated
movements.bound: one frame per event, no log streaming in either direction (docs/architecture/26 section 4)
movements.onOverflow: the subscriber reconnects and re-reads status; a missed event is never a state change
movements.check: LIVE-13 owns the reconnect; docs/architecture/36 owns the catalogue

movements.payload: a masked, size-bounded snapshot for support
movements.onOverflow: truncation is refused rather than performed silently -- an unbounded dump is a crash and an unmasked one is a leak

movements.payload: the synced subset of the envelope, after the strip set has run: no headers, no auth, no body, no token
movements.bound: the browser account sync quota, and the remote's own quota, which the legacy code answers by disabling profiles
movements.onOverflow: the last-good set stays and the failure becomes durable status (the master prompt's subscription rule)
movements.check: LIVE-22 is the storage-and-transit grep; the payload shape is asserted by syncExcludedValueKeys coverage below
movements.note: This is the movement SEC-1 was about, and the one place where 'it is only a reference' is not yet true: see the zeroOmegaSync row, whose token still leaves this machine today.

movements.payload: the pinned Core asset, verified before it is made executable
movements.bound: sizeBytes bounded by the pin document
movements.onOverflow: IntegrityMismatch means refusing to start, not starting and warning (ADR-0019 rule 4)
